analysis:
The PR has two changes. First, SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift (hunk at lines 31-43) changes retireIndexedEntries. Before, one removalLock hold retired the whole URL batch. Now SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices takes the lock once per slice (16 files, per the doc) and calls remove(urls: slice, ...) on each. The guard `hasSafeRoot, ownsEvictionRoot` is still evaluated inside every slice, so a store that has closed or lost its epoch ownership mid-batch stops. The new doc text says a refusal ends the batch. Second, docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md changes the date and the 'Owned retirement coordination' row at line 377 to describe the slicing.

Security-relevant behavior stays unchanged: retirement still goes through remove(...) with the epoch store and root checks, and no DBK3 format, key, HMAC tag derivation, TTL or budget values changed. That keeps the T-041 mitigations (TTL/LRU purge, KEK-derived tags, 1800s TTL) intact. The sliced retirement is an availability improvement, since submit-thread lookups and donor index publication wait on short holds (T-041, TB-007). The cost is that retirement is no longer atomic across the batch. Concurrent writers or epoch changes can interleave between slices, and each slice rechecks ownership and the durable epoch binding (per the doc) so this should fail closed. That nuance cannot be verified here: the removeInSlices and SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove implementations are not in the supplied evidence. Open questions for integration: whether removeInSlices stops on nil, as the doc says, and whether it aggregates externalChange correctly. The first matters because a nil result from an ownership refusal must not be treated as success, or later TTL/budget enforcement could be skipped silently. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
